records.Concise description: A Bitcoin-focused multisig wallet emphasizing user-controlled keys, Miniscript-based recovery/inheritance policies and community-led open-source development.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin Keeper provides multisig vault coordination, hardware-wallet integration and inheritance/recovery configurations. Its current community-led model states that users hold the spending keys and that Keeper cannot unilaterally move funds. Advanced policies can use Miniscript/timelocks and optional server-assisted recovery components without giving the server a unilateral spending quorum.
records.Launch / history: Developed in the early 2020s and transitioned to a community-led/open-source model; current multisig and inheritance functionality remained active in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Keeper adds a distinct policy-driven approach to multisig and inheritance, especially where timelocks/Miniscript encode recovery conditions rather than relying only on organizational procedures.
Important technical or cultural characte: Optional server-assisted recovery without unilateral server spending authority
records.Verification basis: Current project-controlled materials and open-source code support active lifecycle, multisig focus and policy-based recovery/inheritance claims.
Research notes / uncertainties: Some plans may use optional service components; public copy should describe the exact quorum rather than treating all configurations identically.
Server-assisted recovery should not be equated with server custody when the server lacks an independent spending quorum.

records.Concise description: A Bitcoin financial-services company whose core vault product uses collaborative multisig so clients retain a unilateral spending path while Unchained holds a backup key.
records.Deeper researched summary: Unchained vaults are collaborative-custody Bitcoin wallets. The standard model uses three keys with two required to spend; clients hold two keys while Unchained typically holds one, so Unchained cannot move bitcoin alone and clients can transact without Unchained. Current offerings extend the model into inheritance, trust/estate structures and more flexible quorums for sophisticated users.
records.Launch / history: Unchained was founded in 2016 and developed collaborative custody as a central product. Vault, inheritance and estate features continued expanding through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Unchained made collaborative custody a mainstream Bitcoin service model: professional assistance can be added without giving the service a unilateral ability to spend client bitcoin.
Important technical or cultural characte: Unchained ordinarily holds one backup key
Expanded quorum options for advanced clients
Mobile account applications now include Android in 2026
records.Verification basis: Current first-party vault and 2026 product documentation verify the client/Unchained key split, inheritance services and active lifecycle.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe Unchained as a conventional custodian: in the standard collaborative vault it lacks enough keys to spend alone.
Specific institutional, IRA, lending or trust structures may introduce legal/service relationships beyond the basic personal vault and should be described separately.

records.Concise description: An assisted self-custody platform using multi-key vaults, hardware keys and a Casa-held recovery key that cannot spend client funds by itself.
records.Deeper researched summary: Casa offers 3-key and 5-key vaults designed to remove single points of failure while keeping clients in control. In a typical 3-key vault, Casa stores one recovery key offline and the user controls the remaining spending path; Casa's one key is insufficient to move funds unilaterally. Current products include inheritance support and guided hardware-wallet integration. Casa supports assets beyond Bitcoin, but its multisig Bitcoin history is central to the ecosystem.
records.Launch / history: Casa was founded in 2018 and became an early consumer-facing multisig security service. Guided vault and inheritance products remained active through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Casa helped turn complex Bitcoin multisig into a guided consumer service and popularized a model where a company can assist recovery without becoming a unilateral custodian.
Important technical or cultural characte: Casa-held recovery key is a minority key
Casa Pay exists separately from the core multisig vault model

Official sources.label: Casa — what is multisig / non-custodial approach

records.Verification basis: Current 2026 Casa support documentation explicitly states the vault quorums, Casa recovery-key role and non-custodial design.
Research notes / uncertainties: Use 'assisted self-custody' or precise quorum language rather than implying Casa holds no keys; Casa does hold a recovery key in supported vaults.
Casa cannot move bitcoin unilaterally in the documented vault model, but product-specific key layouts should still be checked before public claims.

records.Entity / project type: hardware signer family / companion wallet ecosystem
records.Concise description: A major multi-chain hardware-signer family whose devices secure Bitcoin private keys in Secure Elements and sign transactions through Ledger's companion software or compatible third-party wallets.
records.Deeper researched summary: Ledger's hardware devices generate and protect private keys within dedicated signing hardware; bitcoin itself remains recorded on the network. Current Ledger signers pair with the Ledger Wallet app and third-party Bitcoin wallets, and current Bitcoin accounts support modern address types including Taproot. Ledger's security model uses proprietary Ledger OS and Secure Element technology; that should be described factually rather than treated as a security rating.
Creators / founders: Ledger — founded in 2014 by eight security/cryptocurrency entrepreneurs and engineers
records.Launch / history: Ledger began in 2014; its early HW1/Nano products were Bitcoin-focused and the company expanded into a broad multi-chain signer family and companion software ecosystem.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Ledger is one of the most widely integrated hardware-signer ecosystems and materially shaped hardware-wallet interoperability across Bitcoin software wallets.
Important technical or cultural characte: Ledger Wallet app on mobile and desktop
Bitcoin app/account support including SegWit and Taproot
Multi-chain product family; Bitcoin is one supported network
Bitcoin application code is open-source while core device OS/secure-element stack is not fully open-source
records.Verification basis: Current Ledger Bitcoin product material plus company history and open Bitcoin application code verify active Bitcoin signing support and product-family scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not say a Ledger device 'stores bitcoin'; it protects private keys and signs transactions.
Do not imply open-source status for the entire Ledger hardware/OS stack; distinguish the open Bitcoin app from proprietary components.
Ledger models are consolidated into one canonical family profile.
